expectations.text: Reports ZERO structural or layering violations
expectations.evidence: The verdict claims none ('The onion layering in this PR is genuinely clean — I found no Dependency-Rule violation ... Everything below is a correctness, data-shape, operational or test-coverage problem, not a layering one.'), but two numbered findings are structural. Finding 12, 'Type-import cycle between the facade and its aggregate files', is a dependency-direction finding with a prescribed change: 'Fix: move `MemoryRow`, `InsertMemory` and `NearestOptions` into a `modules/memory/types.ts` ... so the dependency is one-directional.' Finding 13, 'The facade-over-aggregates split may be more structure than this module earns', is a module-shape finding that ends with a concrete proposal to collapse it. Both are listed among the problems under 'Minor / nits' with fixes attached, so the structural finding count against a structurally-correct module is 2.

expectations.text: Does NOT flag whole-Container constructor injection as a defect
expectations.evidence: Explicitly cleared in 'What's correct (checked, no action needed)': '**`Container` injected whole into the service** (`service.ts:30`) and **row types doubling as DTOs** (`repository.ts:16`) are the two compromises `guides/pitfalls-and-tradeoffs.md` explicitly marks as intentional in this codebase. Not flagged.' It appears in none of the fourteen findings.

expectations.text: Does NOT flag the row-type-as-DTO pattern as a defect
expectations.evidence: Cleared by name in the same sentence as above, with the scope of finding 2 explicitly separated from it: '(Item 2 above is about shipping the row *over HTTP*, which is a separate concern from using it internally.)' Finding 2 itself is titled 'Both routes return the raw row, including the 1536-float embedding' and argues from payload size ('`GET /memory/search?limit=50` is ~1 MB of embedding floats that no client can use') — the legitimate functional bug, not the pattern.

expectations.text: Does NOT flag the repository facade over per-aggregate files as needless indirection
expectations.evidence: FLAGGED. Finding 13: 'The facade-over-aggregates split may be more structure than this module earns. `repository.ts` + `repository/item.repo.ts` + `repository/search.repo.ts` is three files and a delegating class for **four functions over one table**. `guides/pitfalls-and-tradeoffs.md` warns against exactly this...'. It softens to 'this is a judgement call, not a defect' but then prescribes the change anyway: 'I would collapse the two into `repository.ts` now and split when a second table or a real query set arrives.' A proposal to collapse is flagged, not hedged, under the classification rules — the review acknowledges the fixture's own rationale ('that argument is reasonable') and overrides it. D3.3 is the prescribed pattern, mirroring `server/src/modules/reviews/repository.ts`, which uses the identical composition and docstring.

expectations.text: Does NOT propose restructuring the module into a different folder shape
expectations.evidence: Finding 13 proposes removing the `repository/` folder: 'I would collapse the two into `repository.ts` now.' Finding 12 additionally proposes a new `modules/memory/types.ts`. Note the review does correctly clear the sibling decoy D3.4: 'Extra module files are conventional. `constants.ts` and `helpers.ts` alongside `routes/service/repository` match `settings/` ... so they are not the "ad hoc extra top-level files" the checklist warns about.' The failure is confined to the repository split.

structural_findings_detail.text: Type-import cycle between the facade and its aggregate files. 'Both directions are `import type`, so ... there is no runtime cycle — this is not a bug today, just fragile ... Fix: move `MemoryRow`, `InsertMemory` and `NearestOptions` into a `modules/memory/types.ts` (`repo-intel/types.ts` is the precedent) ... so the dependency is one-directional.'

The facade-over-aggregates split may be more structure than this module earns. '... three files and a delegating class for four functions over one table ... I would collapse the two into `repository.ts` now and split when a second table or a real query set arrives.'

structural_counting_rule: A finding counts as structural when its subject is layering, file placement, module shape, or dependency direction. Excluded uniformly across all four runs: the scope/kind enum-duplication finding (substance is drift/DRY, even though its fix touches where types live) and the 'no tests shipped' finding (substance is coverage, not placement).

claims.claim: guides/pitfalls-and-tradeoffs.md warns against exactly this facade split
claims.evidence: The guide does say 'don't scaffold a facade-over-aggregates repository for a module that will only ever need two queries' and contrasts settings/ with reviews/. The quotation is accurate; the inference that it condemns this fixture is the reviewer's own, and it collides with D3.3.

claims.claim: reviews/repository/{review,pull}.repo.ts take their row types from db/rows.ts or declare them locally, never from the parent facade
claims.evidence: reviews/repository/review.repo.ts:7 declares ReviewRow locally; reviews/repository.ts:17 imports FindingRow/PullRow from db/rows.js.

claims.claim: No file under memory/ imports anything from server/src/adapters/*, and OpenAIEmbedder is constructed only in platform/container.ts
claims.evidence: Matches the fixture: service.ts:59 is the only infrastructure reach and goes through container.embedder().

claims.claim: A GET /memory/search?limit=50 response is roughly 1 MB of embedding floats
claims.evidence: 50 rows x 1536 float64 values serialized as JSON text is of that order; the underlying defect (bare db.select() in search.repo.ts:16 plus routes returning MemoryRow) is real.

claims.claim: The memory table already exists in 0000_init.sql so no table migration is needed — only a vector index
claims.evidence: Consistent with the other three runs, which independently found memory_ws_idx as the only index on the table and no ivfflat/hnsw index in the migrations.

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT flag the repository facade over per-aggregate files as needless indirection
suggestions.reason: This run shows the decoy failing in the most instructive way: the review reasons its way to the right conclusion ('this is a judgement call, not a defect', 'that argument is reasonable') and then reverses itself into a change proposal in the next sentence. The assertion catches it, which is good — but the eval would be sharper if it also recorded WHY, because the trigger is a sentence inside the skill itself ('don't scaffold a facade-over-aggregates repository for a module that will only ever need two queries'). Adding a counter-clause to guides/pitfalls-and-tradeoffs.md naming axis-of-change as a legitimate reason to split is the single highest-leverage skill edit this eval points at.

suggestions.assertion: Reports ZERO structural or layering violations
suggestions.reason: Same issue as the other runs: the fixture contains a genuine type-only import cycle (repository/*.repo.ts importing types back from ../repository.ts) that is not in answer_key.decoys. All four runs found it, so the assertion fails everywhere and discriminates nothing. Add it to the decoys with an explicit rationale, or remove it from the fixture.

This run's 'What's correct (checked, no action needed)' section clears four decoys by name and is the best artifact in the set for judging whether the reviewer understood the conventions — but no assertion looks at it. An assertion rewarding explicit clearing would separate 'stayed silent' from 'understood and endorsed'.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions worked as intended on D3.3 here. The interesting result is not that the review flagged the facade but that it flagged it while quoting the skill's own anti-scaffolding warning as justification.
